   172	/-! ## The subline distribution -/
   173	
   174	/-- A tuple consisting of an extended line and its projected X and Z lines. -/
   175	abbrev SubLineTriple (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   176	  DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ×
   177	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   178	
   179	/-- An extended line tuple together with a point sampled uniformly on it. -/
   180	abbrev SubLinePointSample (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   181	  SubLineTriple P ×
   182	    (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m -> DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
   183	
   184	/-- The shared restricted line kind and two coordinate indices in one mixture
   185	component of the subline law. -/
   186	abbrev SubLineComponent (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   187	  LineKind × (Fin P.m × Fin P.m)
   188	
   189	/-- Select the restricted line-point distribution of a given kind and index. -/
   190	noncomputable def restrictedLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   191	    (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
   192	    Distribution (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   193	  match kind with
   194	  | .axis => restrictedALineDist P.toLdParams i
   195	  | .diagonal => restrictedDLineDist P.toLdParams i
   196	
   197	/-- Sample a subline tuple and then a uniform affine parameter on its
   198	extended line. -/
   199	noncomputable def subLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   200	    (D : Distribution (SubLineTriple P)) :
   201	    Distribution (SubLinePointSample P) :=
   202	  (Distribution.prod D
   203	    (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).map fun sample =>
   204	      (sample.1, sample.1.1.base + sample.2 • sample.1.1.direction)
   205	
   206	/-- Retain the projected line pair and the X projection of an extended point. -/
   207	def subLineXProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (sample : SubLinePointSample P) :
   208	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   209	      (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) :=
   210	  (sample.1.2, projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   211	
   212	/-- Retain the projected line pair and the Z projection of an extended point. -/
   213	def subLineZProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (sample : SubLinePointSample P) :
   214	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   215	      (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) :=
   216	  (sample.1.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   217	
   218	/-- The X-point marginal associated with one restricted product component. -/
   219	noncomputable def subLineXComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   220	    (component : SubLineComponent P) :
   221	    Distribution
   222	      ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   223	        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   224	  (Distribution.prod
   225	    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1)
   226	    ((restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.2).map Prod.fst)).map
   227	      fun sample => ((sample.1.1, sample.2), sample.1.2)
   228	
   229	/-- The Z-point marginal associated with one restricted product component. -/
   230	noncomputable def subLineZComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   231	    (component : SubLineComponent P) :
   232	    Distribution
   233	      ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   234	        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   235	  (Distribution.prod
   236	    ((restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1).map Prod.fst)
   237	    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.2)).map
   238	      fun sample => ((sample.1, sample.2.1), sample.2.2)
   239	
   240	/-- The subline distribution of `lem:qld-sublines`, paper lines 1063--1069.
   241	Its source-mixture field records the X and Z point marginals separately; it
   242	does not assert a joint conditional law for the pair of projected points. -/
   243	structure SubLineWitness (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   244	  /-- The actual distribution of an extended line and two projected lines. -/
   245	  D : Distribution (SubLineTriple P)
   246	  /-- The distribution has total mass one. -/
   247	  isProbability : D.IsProbability
   248	  /-- Its extended-line marginal is the direct line-point marginal. -/
   249	  extended_marginal : D.map Prod.fst =
   250	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst
   251	  /-- Every point of an extended line projects onto both stored source lines. -/
   252	  incidence : ∀ sample ∈ D.support, ∀ u ∈ sample.1.pointSet,
   253	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.1.pointSet ∧
   254	      projZ (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.2.pointSet
   255	  /-- Each line triple carries affine data sufficient for
   256	  `combineLinePoly_spec`. -/
   257	  compatibility : ∀ sample ∈ D.support,
   258	    ∃ aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta : PauliScalar P,
   259	      IsCombineLineCompatible
   260	        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.base)
   261	        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.direction)
   262	        sample.2.1.base sample.2.1.direction
   263	        sample.2.2.base sample.2.2.direction
   264	        aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta
   265	  /-- Each one-point projected marginal is a mixture of restricted product
   266	  laws.  No equality for their joint conditional law is claimed. -/
   267	  source_mixture : ∃ components : Distribution (SubLineComponent P),
   268	    components.IsProbability ∧
   269	      (subLinePointDist P D).map subLineXProjection =
   270	        Distribution.bind components (subLineXComponentDist P) ∧
   271	      (subLinePointDist P D).map subLineZProjection =
   272	        Distribution.bind components (subLineZComponentDist P)
   273	  /-- An extended axis line has axis-parallel projected lines. -/
   274	  axis_closure : ∀ sample ∈ D.support, sample.1.kind = .axis ->
   275	    sample.2.1.kind = .axis ∧ sample.2.2.kind = .axis
   276	
   277	/-! ## Extended lines and global polynomial pairs -/
   278	
   279	/-- Extended-line POVMs and directly indexed, completed-answer forms of the two
   280	consistency relations in `lem:qld-4-13`, paper lines 1020--1034. The direct line
   281	carrier avoids the dimension-divisibility obstruction documented in
   282	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. -/
   283	structure ExtendedLinesWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
   284	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
   285	    (δ : ℝ) where
   286	  /-- The complete extended-line measurement on each player side. -/
   287	  Qline : (side : PlayerSide) -> DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ->
   288	    Measurement (DirectDegPoly P.extendedDirectLd (P.m * P.d + 1))
   289	      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   290	  /-- Axis-line outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
   291	  axis_degree : ∀ side line f, line.kind = .axis ->
   292	    Not (∀ i, P.d < i.val -> f i = 0) ->
   293	      (Qline side line).effect f = 0
   294	  /-- Alice's evaluated line measurement is consistent with Bob's completed
   295	  combined point measurement. -/
   296	  consistent_alice : consistencyDefect
   297	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd)
   298	    (fun sample answer => S.place .AA'
   299	      (((Qline .alice sample.1).postprocess
   300	        (fun f => (directEvalOpt sample.1 sample.2 f).map
   301	          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P))).effect answer))
   302	    (fun sample answer => S.place .BA''
   303	      (((points.Q .bob
   304	        (projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   305	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))).postprocess fun ab =>
   306	          some (directPointToPauli P sample.2 (alphaVar P.m) * ab.1 +
   307	            directPointToPauli P sample.2 (betaVar P.m) * ab.2)).effect answer))
   308	    S.psiHat <= δ
   309	  /-- Bob's evaluated line measurement is consistent with Alice's completed
   310	  combined point measurement. -/
   311	  consistent_bob : consistencyDefect
   312	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd)
   313	    (fun sample answer => S.place .BB'
   314	      (((Qline .bob sample.1).postprocess
   315	        (fun f => (directEvalOpt sample.1 sample.2 f).map
   316	          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P))).effect answer))
   317	    (fun sample answer => S.place .AB''
   318	      (((points.Q .alice
   319	        (projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   320	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))).postprocess fun ab =>
   321	          some (directPointToPauli P sample.2 (alphaVar P.m) * ab.1 +
   322	            directPointToPauli P sample.2 (betaVar P.m) * ab.2)).effect answer))
   323	    S.psiHat <= δ
   324	
   325	/-- The side-indexed global polynomial-pair measurements handed to Chapter 16.
   326	This is the exact conclusion of `lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1267--1274, with
   327	the two heterogeneous point-consistency displays stated separately. -/
   328	structure GlobalPairWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
   329	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (δ : ℝ) where
   330	  /-- The complete global polynomial-pair measurement on each player side. -/
   331	  Smeas : (side : PlayerSide) ->
   332	    Measurement (PolyPair P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   333	  /-- Both global polynomial-pair measurements are projective. -/
   334	  projective : ∀ side, Measurement.IsProjective (Smeas side)
   335	  /-- Alice's global evaluations are consistent with Bob's source point
   336	  measurements, for each Pauli basis. -/
   337	  point_consistent_alice : ∀ W : PauliKind,
   338	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))
   339	      (fun u a => S.place .AA'
   340	        (((Smeas .alice).postprocess (evalAt W u)).effect a))
   341	      (fun u a => S.place .BA''
   342	        ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect a))
   343	      S.psiHat <= δ
   344	  /-- Bob's global evaluations are consistent with Alice's source point
   345	  measurements, for each Pauli basis. -/
   346	  point_consistent_bob : ∀ W : PauliKind,
   347	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))
   348	      (fun u a => S.place .BB'
   349	        (((Smeas .bob).postprocess (evalAt W u)).effect a))
   350	      (fun u a => S.place .AB''
   351	        ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a))
   352	      S.psiHat <= δ
   353	
   354	end

  1046	\label{sec:apply-ldt}

  1048	The combined point and line measurements of the previous two sections are next
  1049	merged into a single measurement returning a pair of global polynomials that
  1050	encode the $X$-basis and the $Z$-basis information simultaneously. This is
  1051	done by encoding the pair as one polynomial in $2m+2$ variables and invoking

  1058	the instantiation step for admissible parameters with $m \ge 2$. The

  1060	analyzed, together with candidate repairs, in

  2075		This is not a named statement of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. It records two
  2076		compression identities between the classical low individual degree game
  2077		and its directly indexed presentation.
  2078	
  2079		Let $(\psi, A, B)$ be a strategy for the classical game with parameters
  2080		$(q,m,d,k)$, and extend it to the directly indexed game by adjoining to
  2081		each player a register of dimension $q/m$, the common size of the
  2082		classes of the index function $\chi$ of

  2084		register are perfectly correlated in the extended state. For a
  2085		polynomial-tuple POVM $G^{\mathrm B}$ on
  2086		$\hilb_{\mathrm B}\ot\C^{q/m}$, let $\bar G^{\mathrm B}$ be the
  2087		normalized average of its diagonal blocks over the residue register.
  2088		Then, over a uniformly random point $u\in\F_q^m$, the off-diagonal
  2089		defect between Alice's point measurement and the evaluation of
  2090		$G^{\mathrm B}$ on the extended strategy equals the defect between
  2091		Alice's original point measurement and the evaluation of
  2092		$\bar G^{\mathrm B}$ on $(\psi,A,B)$.

  2095		$\hilb_{\mathrm A}\ot\C^{q/m}$, compression gives equality between
  2096		the extended polynomial/point defect and the defect between the
  2097		evaluation of $\bar G^{\mathrm A}$ and Bob's original point
  2098		measurement. No projectivity hypothesis is imposed on the strategy or
  2099		on either polynomial-tuple POVM.
  2100	\end{lemma}

  2104		amplification of the original point measurement, while polynomial
  2105		evaluation commutes with averaging the diagonal blocks. The quadratic
  2106		form of the correlated state against each mixed pair of operators is
  2107		therefore the quadratic form of the original state against the
  2108		compressed pair, and summing the off-diagonal terms gives both identities.
  2109	\end{proof}

   741	Since only admissible field sizes $q = 2^k$ arise in the Pauli basis test, the
   742	maximally entangled state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ and the qudit Pauli
   743	projectors are isomorphic to tensor products of qubit EPR states
   744	$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}$ and qubit Pauli projectors. This is the content of the
   745	next lemma, which is what allows the Pauli basis test to self-test Pauli
   746	observables and maximally entangled states over \emph{qubits}
   747	(Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}).
   748	
   749	\begin{lemma}[Qudit-to-qubit isomorphism]\label{lem:pauli-binary}
   750		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.qubitPauliProj, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_qubitIsometry}
   751		\leanok
   752		\uses{def:admissible-size, def:subfields-kappa, def:binary-representation,
   753			def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR}
   754		For all admissible field sizes $q = 2^k$ and integers $L \ge 0$, there
   755		exists an isomorphism $\phi : (\C^q)^{\ot L} \to (\C^2)^{\ot Lk}$ such that
   756		\begin{equation}\label{eq:epr-q-to-epr-2}
   757			\phi \ot \phi\, \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot L}
   758			= \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot Lk}
   759		\end{equation}
   760		(applying the natural identifications between
   761		$(\C^q)^{\ot L} \ot (\C^q)^{\ot L}$ and $(\C^q \ot \C^q)^{\ot L}$, and
   762		between $(\C^2)^{\ot Lk} \ot (\C^2)^{\ot Lk}$ and
   763		$(\C^2 \ot \C^2)^{\ot Lk}$). Moreover, for all $W \in \{X, Z\}$ and all
   764		$u \in \F_q^L$,
   765		\begin{equation}\label{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}
   766			\tau^W_u = \phi^\dagger\,
   767			\Bigl(\bigotimes_{i=1}^L \bigotimes_{j=1}^k
   768			\sigma^W_{u_{ij}}\Bigr)\, \phi\;.
   769		\end{equation}
   770		Here $(u_{ij})_{i,j}$ is the array of $\F_2$ values with
   771		$u_i = \sum_j u_{ij} e_j$ for all $i \in \{1, \dots, L\}$, where
   772		$\{e_1, \dots, e_k\}$ is the fixed self-dual normal basis of $\F_q$ over
   773		$\F_2$ of Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}; and for
   774		$i \in \{1, \dots, L\}$ and $j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$ the $(i,j)$-th factor
   775		$\sigma^W_{u_{ij}}$ denotes the projector
   776		$\frac{1}{2}\bigl(\Id + (-1)^{u_{ij}} \sigma^W(1)\bigr)$ acting on the
   777		$s$-th qubit, where $s = (i-1)k + j$.
   778		We index the product coordinates from zero: values $(i-1,j-1)$ correspond to
   779		the paper's pair $(i,j)$.  The corrected upper bound $j\leq k$ is
   780		documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_pauli-binary-factor-index}.
   781	\end{lemma}
   782	\begin{proof}
   783		\leanok
   784		\uses{def:binary-representation, def:subfields-kappa, lem:downsize_field,
   785			def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR, lem:pauli-observable-expansion}
   786		Let
   787		$e : \F_q^L \to \F_2^{L \times k}$ be the bijection that expands each
   788		coordinate in the fixed self-dual normal basis
   789		(Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}), so that $e(u)$ is exactly the
   790		array $(u_{ij})_{i,j}$ of the statement, and let $\phi$ be the unitary that
   791		permutes the two computational bases along $e$, that is,
   792		$\phi \ket{u} = \ket{e(u)}$. Identity \eqref{eq:epr-q-to-epr-2} holds for
   793		any such relabelling: a bijection of orthonormal bases carries the maximally
   794		entangled state of the source space to that of the target space. For
   795		\eqref{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}, conjugation by $\phi^\dagger$ is exactly
   796		the reindexing of a matrix along $e$, so it suffices to compare matrix
   797		entries. Both generalized Pauli observables are computed entrywise from
   798		Definition~\ref{def:generalized-pauli}: $\tau^W(a)$ is, for $W = X$, the
   799		permutation matrix of the translation $y \mapsto y + a$, and, for $W = Z$,
   800		the diagonal matrix with entries $(-1)^{\tr(a \cdot y)}$. The relabelling
   801		$e$ is additive, and item 2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} gives
   802		$\tr(a \cdot y) = e(a) \cdot e(y)$ by self-duality of the basis; the two
   803		entry formulas are therefore carried by the reindexing to the corresponding
   804		formulas over $\F_2$, so that $\tau^W(a)$ becomes $\tau^W(e(a))$ for both
   805		$W$. Finally, the projectors are recovered from the observables by the
   806		inversion identity \eqref{eq:pauli-inversion-0} in its characteristic-two
   807		form $\tau^W_u = \E_{\ba} (-1)^{\tr(\ba \cdot u)}\, \tau^W(\ba)$, used
   808		over $\F_q^L$ on the left-hand side and over $\F_2^{L \times k}$ on the
   809		right; averaging the entrywise comparison
   810		over $\ba$ carries $\tau^W_u$ to the qubit projector at the label
   811		$e(u) = \kappa(u)$, which is \eqref{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}. This is the
   812		characteristic-two specialization of
   813		Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-observable-expansion}; the corresponding general-prime
   814		expansion and inversion are discussed in
   815		\cite{gap:qpbt_characteristic-two-pauli-scope}. The argument uses neither
   816		the qudit-by-qudit isometry $\theta$ of the source
   817		proof nor the product and twisted-commutation relations of
   818		Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation}.
   819	\end{proof}
   820	
   821	\begin{remark}\label{rem:pauli-binary-source}
   822		In the source statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-binary} in
   823		\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}, the index range of the qubit factor is printed as
   824		$j \in \{1, \dots, q\}$; the intended range, used above, is
   825		$j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, as the $i$-th qudit is mapped to $k$ qubits. The
   826		source also quantifies over arbitrary integers $L$; the statement above
   827		takes $L$ to be a natural number, including zero, and uses the usual
   828		empty-product convention for the tensor powers when $L=0$.  The index
   829		correction is documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_pauli-binary-factor-index}.
   830	\end{remark}

\chapter{Combining the bases and applying the classical test}
\label{chap:qpbt-combining}
% Paper subsection label sec:combining kept for cross-reference fidelity; the
% companion label sec:apply-ldt is attached to the corresponding section below.
% Source: references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex,
% lines 680-1414 (subsections "Combining the X and Z measurements" and
% "Applying the classical low-degree test").
\label{sec:combining}

Throughout this chapter we work in the setting of
Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}: a projective strategy for the Pauli basis
test game succeeds with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all operators act
relative to the expanded state $\ket{\hat\psi}$ on registers
$\mathsf{A}\,\mathsf{A}'\,\mathsf{A}''\,\mathsf{B}\,\mathsf{B}'\,\mathsf{B}''$
(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state}), where each of the four ancilla
registers $\mathsf{A}'$, $\mathsf{A}''$, $\mathsf{B}'$, and $\mathsf{B}''$
--- two appended per player, the pair $\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''$
(respectively $\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''$) holding $M$ EPR pairs of local
dimension $q$ --- is a register of $M = 2^m$ qudits with Hilbert space
isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$.
We write $q = 2^t$ (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) and
$\tr:\F_q\to\F_2$ for the subfield trace. The points measurements
$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-measurement}), their binary refinements
\[
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r}_b
	= \sum_{a \,:\, \tr(ar) = b} \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\,,
	\qquad r \in \F_q,\ b \in \F_2
\]
(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-trace-projection}), and the lines
measurements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{f}$
(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-line-measurement}) are those constructed in
Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}, and $\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}(\eps)$ and
$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)$ denote the error functions of
Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons} and Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-line-cons},
respectively.

A subscript such as $(\,\cdot\,)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}$ indicates the pair of
registers on which an operator acts; the two bipartitions in use are
$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ versus $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ and
$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$ versus $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$. The state-dependent
distances $\approx_\delta$ (Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}) and
$\simeq_\delta$ (Definition~\ref{def:consistency}) are taken with respect to
$\ket{\hat\psi}$ and averaged over the stated question distribution, and
``all symmetric equivalents'' of an approximation is meant in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}. Between scalars, $\alpha
\approx_\delta \beta$ means $|\alpha - \beta| \le O(\delta)$. For sums of
measurement operators over outcomes satisfying a predicate we use the bracket
notation of Definition~\ref{def:bracket}; for instance
$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a,\ \mathrm{eval}_z(\cdot)=b]}
= \sum_{f_X,f_Z \,:\, f_X(x)=a,\ f_Z(z)=b} T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}$.
For a line $\ell$ (Definition~\ref{def:line}) and $k \in \N$ we write
$\deg_k(\ell)$ for the set of polynomial functions on $\ell$ of degree at most
$k$ in the line parameter, and
$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q) = \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$
(Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}) for the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$. Elements of
$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ enter the statements and proofs of this chapter
only through the representatives themselves and their evaluations; evaluation
identifies the representatives with the induced polynomial functions
(Definition~\ref{def:polynomials-degree}), bijectively precisely when
$d \le q-1$, a bound that admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ does not imply and that
is not assumed here. The restriction of an element of
$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ to a line has total degree at most $md$.

\section{Combined point measurements}

The measurements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}$ and
$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}$ commute only approximately. The first goal of
this chapter is to construct a single projective measurement that
simultaneously measures both, first at points and then along lines. The
construction of the combined point measurement proceeds in three steps: the
binary refinements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}$ and
$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}$ are combined into a sandwich POVM, the
resulting family is shown to satisfy an approximate linearity in the index
pair $(r,s)$, and the following result of Natarajan and
Vidick~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity} converts approximate linearity into exact
linearity, from which a projective measurement with outcomes in $\F_q^2$ is
assembled by Fourier averaging.

directly indexed question carrier and line-point law documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, and the completed answer
alphabet documented in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-lines-error-term.tex`.
Their conversion to the source's verifier game remains open. This declaration takes
an already constructed point witness; the companion obligation below supplies that
witness existentially.
-/
theorem exists_extendedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness :
    ∃ deltaCombine : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ, IsPolyErr₂ deltaCombine ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε δQ : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
        (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ),
        Nonempty (ExtendedLinesWitness S points
          (deltaCombine ((P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * ε)
            ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) / (P.q : ℝ)))) := by
  sorry

/-! The following directly indexed obligation supplies the point witness from
`lem:qld-4-10` rather than taking it as an external hypothesis. -/

/-- Directly indexed extended-line obligation with the numerical error expression
printed in `lem:qld-4-13`, paper lines 1020--1034.

The `_ofPointsWitness` companion assumes a point witness, while this declaration
supplies one existentially. Both declarations use the directly indexed questions,
law, and completed answer alphabet, so neither is the source-facing paper statement. -/
theorem exists_extendedLinesWitness :
    ∃ deltaQ : ℝ → ℝ, IsPolyErr deltaQ ∧
      ∃ deltaCombine : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ, IsPolyErr₂ deltaCombine ∧
        ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε),
          ∃ points : CombinedPointsWitness S (deltaQ ε),
            Nonempty (ExtendedLinesWitness S points
              (deltaCombine ((P.m : ℝ) ^ 2 * ε)
                ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) / (P.q : ℝ)))) := by
  sorry

/-- Construction of the extended-line measurements with the estimate actually
delivered by the first proof route, `C * m * poly(epsilon, md / q)`.

This is an established auxiliary form of the argument, not the source-labelled
`lem:qld-4-13`; it must not be advertised as that theorem. The source discrepancy
is analyzed in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-lines-error-term.tex`. As in the
companion directly indexed declaration, the extended questions use the directly
indexed line-space construction. This conditional declaration takes an already
constructed point witness; the obligation below supplies it existentially. Relating
its game to the source's seed-bearing game requires the transport and soundness
obligations in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
-/
theorem exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∃ deltaCombine : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ, IsPolyErr₂ deltaCombine ∧
        ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε δQ : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
          (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ),
          Nonempty (ExtendedLinesWitness S points
            (C * (P.m : ℝ) *
              deltaCombine ε ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) / (P.q : ℝ)))) := by
  sorry

/-- Directly indexed construction for the auxiliary estimate
`C * m * poly(epsilon, md / q)`. This has the same directly indexed estimate as
`exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness`, with the point witness
existentially supplied rather than assumed.
/-- Construction of the projective global polynomial-pair measurements from
`lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1267--1274.  The statement has the source's universal
constants and contains no divisibility hypothesis or residual construction input.

The argument uses low-degree soundness at dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The current
direct carrier realizes the required dimension without assuming
`2 * m + 2 ∣ q`, but it does not itself prove the game-correspondence and
auxiliary-parameter estimates required by the soundness import; those obligations
are exposed by `exists_direct_ld_soundness` and documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.  Absorption of the established
combined-lines prefactor into the final universal constants is to use
`deltaQld_mono` on its stated source parameter domain.
-/
theorem exists_globalPairWitness :
    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
        ∀ S : ProjectiveSetting P ε,
          Nonempty (GlobalPairWitness S (deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q)) := by
  sorry

end
